entryPoint: SLA::priorityEscalation() in include/class.sla.php (lines 116-118) — instance method with no parameters; reads the bound SLA object's in-memory flags property and returns the evaluated expression `$this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE`.
coreLogic: Self-contained inline expression in SLA::priorityEscalation() — no delegation to other methods. Reads `$this->flags` (integer bitmask persisted in SLA_TABLE.flags). Uses logical AND (`&&`) with constant SLA::FLAG_ESCALATE (0x0002), not bitwise AND (`&`) and not SLA::hasFlag(). Related flag plumbing in the same class (not called by priorityEscalation): getInfo() (lines 73-79) exposes `enable_priority_escalation` as `$this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE`; update() (lines 168-192) rebuilds `$this->flags` from form vars via `($vars['isactive'] ? self::FLAG_ACTIVE : 0) | ($vars['disable_overdue_alerts']) | ($vars['enable_priority_escalation']) | ($vars['transient'])` then persists via save() — note enable_priority_escalation lacks the isset()-to-flag normalization used for disable_overdue_alerts and transient; SLA::hasFlag($flag) (lines 102-104) reads via `$this->get('flags', 0) & $flag`. Initial seed data sets flags:3 (active + escalate) in include/i18n/en_US/sla.yaml.
inputShape: No parameters and no by-reference arguments. Operates on the bound SLA instance; reads `$this->flags` (integer, already loaded on the model from SLA_TABLE.flags). Does not mutate the instance or any caller-supplied objects.
outputShape: Undeclared scalar return. Truthy when `$this->flags` is non-zero (expression evaluates to integer 2, the value of FLAG_ESCALATE); falsy when `$this->flags` is 0 (expression evaluates to 0). This is a boolean return contract in practice (callers would treat it truthy/falsy), but the raw return value is the evaluated expression, not an explicit (bool) cast. Important: this differs from getInfo()['enable_priority_escalation'], which is truthy only when bit 0x0002 is set — e.g. flags=1 (active only) yields truthy here but falsy in getInfo().
sideEffects: Reads `$this->flags` from the in-memory SLA VerySimpleModel instance only — no database query, no lazy-load of related models (_schedule/_config are untouched), no global state ($cfg not accessed), no Signal::send, no file I/O, no caching writes, no mutation of $this or external state
constraints: Preserve the exact expression `$this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE` (logical AND with constant 0x0002); do not substitute `$this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE` or `$this->hasFlag(self::FLAG_ESCALATE)` — those would change observable behavior for flags values where only non-escalation bits are set (e.g. flags=1 returns truthy today)
SLA::FLAG_ESCALATE constant is 0x0002; stored as bit 2 in SLA_TABLE.flags (default 3 = FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE per install-mysql.sql)
flags=0 edge case must return falsy (0)
Method signature must remain unchanged: public instance method, zero parameters, same return type behavior
Extractor service must delegate to this existing flag-read expression; do not reimplement bitmask semantics with different operators
No new database writes, global reads, or side effects beyond the single in-memory flags property read documented above

getInfo()/update() enable_priority_escalation paths use bitwise AND and form-var OR respectively — related for admin persistence but outside priorityEscalation() call chain; parity harness targets priorityEscalation() return values, not getInfo() unless separately scoped
harnessInputShape: JSON object with: flags (integer, SLA flags bitmask loaded onto a hydrated SLA instance — use 3 for escalation-enabled with FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE, 1 for FLAG_ACTIVE only without FLAG_ESCALATE, 0 for the flags=0 edge case). Harness bootstraps via main.inc.php, constructs SLA via SLA::__hydrate(['flags' => flags]), calls priorityEscalation(), and JSON-encodes the raw return value.
